header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (QuantifyAI), Derek Owens (QuantifyAI), Monica Li (QuantifyAI), Evan Torres (QuantifyAI)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quantization experiment results (INT8 vs FP8), discuss quality impact, perf deltas, and next steps for benchmarking and security review. Customer saw modest latency improvements with INT8 but noted small quality regressions on hallucination-prone prompts; FP8 remains promising but with less maturity on stack. Action items assigned for deeper runs and infra traces.
topics: Next steps for canary and benchmark plan
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone good afternoon thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45, quick roll call.
[00:10] Rachel: yep rachel here, thanks.
[00:15] Derek: derek on my side.
[00:20] Monica: monica here.
[00:30] Alex: cool, agenda today - quick results review of the int8 and fp8 runs priya will share perf deltas and then we'll go over any security concerns and next steps.
[01:05] Priya: ok thanks alex, I'll start with the summary of runs - we ran the 7B variant on dedicated infra and on our hosted nodes, int8 quant had about 1.9x token throughput improvement versus fp16 baseline and tail latency improvements of ~25% p95. fp8 experiments showed similar throughput to int8 in some shards but variability higher, seems kernel maturity is affecting consistency.
[01:50] Rachel: quick q - how are you measuring quality? are we using exact Rouge or our internal correctness checks?
[02:05] Priya: we're using the eval harness you provided plus a synthetic QA set - rouge/bleu-like metrics and then a custom hallucination score. int8 dropped on hallucination-sensitive prompts by about 2-3% absolute, most other metrics within noise.
[02:40] Evan: can you remind us what 2-3% means in user impact? is it noticeable in prod?
[02:55] Samir: yeah usually 2-3% on hallucination metric can surface as a higher rate of false assertions on critical prompts, we flagged a few examples in the artifacts link (see notes). that said latency gains are substantial and cost per token drops ~40% in our rough calc.
[03:30] Derek: what about fp8, is the quality better than int8?
[03:40] Priya: fp8 tends to preserve fp16-like quality on many workloads but we saw some instability on longer context lengths - fp8 kernels on some GPU stacks are still experimental; you might get slightly better accuracy but less predictable p95 latency.
[04:05] Rachel: any change in perplexity or token distribution we should watch?
[04:15] Priya: small uptick in perplexity for int8 on the QA set, again concentrated on certain token patterns, seems quantization noise under specific attention heads.
[04:40] Alex: okay can we walk through perf numbers you ran against the canary workload?
[04:50] Priya: sure - baseline fp16: avg latency 220ms/token, p95 480ms. int8: avg 115ms/token, p95 360ms. fp8: avg 120ms/token, p95 410ms but with wider variance between shards.
[05:30] Derek: those p95 deltas are useful - what about warm vs cold starts and kv cache behaviour?
[05:40] Priya: kv cache behavior is consistent; int8 benefits more on sustained throughput when cache hit rate is high. cold starts are similar across formats because model load and compilation dominate. we did see fp8 compilation fallback on one node which caused a spike.
[06:10] Monica: security question - are any of these quantized artifacts stored differently? we need to ensure encryption at rest and key usage (HSM/KMS) still applies.
[06:25] Alex: yes all artifacts in Redwood Dedicated are encrypted and we can integrate with your KMS. priya any notes?
[06:35] Priya: quantized model files are stored as blobs in the same artifact store, nothing special, we tag them, access is RBAC controlled, we will include the checksum and provenance in the artifact metadata for audits.
[07:00] Monica: great, i'll need the security addendum and a quick mapping to our compliance control list (SOC2 controls).
[07:10] Alex: we'll share the doc.
[07:20] Rachel: in the examples you flagged, can you show one that regressed under int8?
[07:30] Priya: yes paging to the example set - for example prompt about product recall the int8 answer included a fabricated date - fp16 was correct. it's subtle but reproducible at scale on that prompt family.
[08:05] Evan: is that something we can mitigate via prompt engineering or instruct fine-tuning?
[08:15] Samir: possibly, we can apply calibrated post-filters or reranking with a smaller fp16 reranker - that's one of the Redwood recommended fallbacks: low-cost int8 for main path, fp16 rerank for high-stakes responses.
[08:45] Derek: what's the cost tradeoff if we rerank critical responses?
[08:55] Priya: our rough calc: main int8 path reduces token cost ~40%, adding fp16 rerank on 5% of responses adds back maybe 6-8% cost, still net savings.
[09:20] Rachel: okay interesting. next, can we talk about long-context 2k token runs? we saw more regressions there.
[09:30] Priya: long context exacerbates quantization noise for some attention operations; int8 shows a larger drop in score for >1k tokens in our tests. fp8 sometimes handles longer context better in quality but as mentioned has higher latency variance.
[10:00] Evan: is that because of kernel tiling or attention numerics?
[10:10] Priya: both - attention normalization and softmax precision interact with quantization; certain kernels tile differently causing rounding differences. we're working with kernel devs to address this.
[10:40] Derek: for our VPC setup, any special networking considerations for dedicated nodes? we saw occasional 50-100ms spikes that we can't account for.
[10:55] Samir: likely egress path or NVLink contention - we'll need your network topology and packet traces. we asked for traces and Derek agreed to supply them.
[11:20] Derek: yes i'll get those, i'll also include a note about our private peering arrangement.
[11:30] Monica: on compliance, can you provide audit logs for model loads and inference access?
[11:40] Alex: yes redwood console gives token-level traces and per-route logs, we can extend retention if needed.
[11:50] Monica: also need encryption key rotation notes.
[11:55] Alex: will include in the package.
[12:05] Priya: quick note on benchmarks - we also ran a customer-specific eval harness with 500 prompts, int8 regressed on 12 prompts, fp8 on 6 prompts. we attached the CSV and example prompts.
[12:40] Rachel: thanks, we'll review those examples and flag which are high-priority.
[12:50] Evan: what's the recommended canary plan if we want to try int8 in prod?
[12:55] Samir: start with a small traffic slice (5-10%), enable fp16 reranker on a safety route, monitor hallucination metric and latencies for 48-72 hours, have an automatic rollback to fp16 if hallucination delta crosses threshold.
[13:30] Derek: can you automate rollback based on a metric?
[13:40] Priya: yes Redwood's routing supports metric-based fallback, we can configure canary + automatic fallback per route.
[14:10] Rachel: timeline - we'd like to pilot in Q4, ideally by mid-October. is that feasible?
[14:20] Alex: yes that's reasonable if we complete the deep runs and security review in next 4-6 weeks.
[14:30] Priya: action items - we'll run the 2k token int8 experiment and share logs, we'll prepare benchmark spreadsheet with cost deltas and example regressions, we'll prepare canary playbook.
[15:00] Monica: i'll review security docs and get back.
[15:10] Derek: i'll send infra traces.
[15:20] Rachel: one last thing - are there known vendor dependencies for fp8 kernel stability?
[15:30] Priya: vendor-dependent optimizations exist; some CUDA/cuDNN flags and driver versions matter, also specific kernel builds from compiler stack. we documented the recommended driver matrix.
[15:55] Alex: ok final recap - Alex to send perf and cost spreadsheet, Priya to run int8 long-context and share logs, Derek to provide traces, Monica to review security addendum. next sync same time next week unless we need an ad-hoc deep-dive. thanks all.
[16:30] Rachel: thanks everyone.
[16:35] All: bye
